name: Linear MDS code main conjecture
question: Do nontrivial linear MDS codes satisfy the predicted length bound except known cases?
dispatch_next: Generalise the arc engine to PG(3,q) with 5-point frames and reproduce known maximum arc sizes for q <= 9.
dispatch_why: The next experiment reproduces known maximum arcs in PG(3,q). The plane k=3 case is already the proved Segre-Bose range.

campaign.method: Exhaustive arc search in projective spaces with frame-fixing symmetry reduction
campaign.hypothesis: A linear [n,k] MDS code over GF(q) with k <= q has n <= q+1, except n = q+2 when q is even and k is 3 or q-1.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Extend from k = 3 (Segre/Bose) to k = 4 arcs in PG(3,q) for small non-prime q (q = 8, 9), certifying maximum arc sizes.
campaign.next_experiment: Generalise the arc engine to PG(3,q) with 5-point frames and reproduce known maximum arc sizes for q <= 9.
campaign.falsification: An explicit n-arc exceeding the bound, verified by exact determinant checks.
campaign.blocker: The conjecture is proved for prime q (Ball 2012); open non-prime cases need far larger searches than k = 3.

probes.name: Linear MDS code main conjecture
probes.title: Maximum arcs in PG(2,q) = longest 3-dimensional linear MDS codes
probes.frontier: Known for k = 3 by Segre (q odd) and Bose (q even); the MDS conjecture is proved for prime q (Ball 2012) and open for general prime powers.

smoke.scope: For q in {2, 3, 4, 5, 7}: an explicit maximum arc and exhaustive exclusion of larger arcs (MDS length bound for k = 3).

deep.scope: For q in {2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9}: an explicit maximum arc and exhaustive exclusion of larger arcs (MDS length bound for k = 3).

milestones.title: Maximum arcs (3-dimensional MDS codes) in PG(2,q) for q = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7
milestones.description: Maximum arc sizes 4, 4, 6, 6, 8 with explicit witnesses and exhaustive exclusion of larger arcs; arcs through a frame recount q-2 conics for odd q. Deep run adds q = 8, 9.
